credentials.description: service ID — the user part of HTTP Basic auth, base64(SERVICE_ID:SECRET_TOKEN)
secret token — the password part of HTTP Basic auth

example_prompt: Get the sender names I'm allowed to use on NimbaSMS.

limit.description: Maximum number of sender names to return.

next.description: URL of the next page, or null.

previous.description: URL of the previous page, or null.

status.description: Sender name status. Only 'accepted' can be used in send_message and send_verification.

added_at.description: Date added, as a Unix timestamp (seconds).

gotchas: Only sender names with status 'accepted' can be used in send_message and send_verification. Valid statuses are 'pending' (under validation), 'refused' (refused) and 'accepted' (usable) — not 'active'.
Sender names are approved manually by NimbaSMS — they cannot be created via the API. Create them from the dashboard, then retrieve them here.
The value returned in 'name' must be used as is in send_message({ sender_name: '...' }) — it is case-sensitive.
The NimbaSMS SDK strips the 'count', 'next', 'previous' fields from the paginated response and returns only 'results'. When calling the API directly, the raw response contains all of these fields.
open_questions: Sandbox: provider.json declares none and no gotcha documents a test environment — every call reaches production.
